articles.title: Volkswagen e Audi anunciam recall global de quase 3 milhões de carros | G1
articles.standfirst: Falha envolve corrosão de um parafuso e pode comprometer o controle da direção, segundo órgão alemão. Alguns dos modelos afetados foram vendidos no Brasil, mas montadoras ainda não informaram se unidades do país estão no recall.
articles.summary: Alguns dos modelos afetados foram vendidos no Brasil, mas montadoras ainda não informaram se unidades do país estão no recall.
articles.body:
Volkswagen Golf VII R — Foto: divulgação/Volkswagen

A Volkswagen e a Audi convocaram um recall global de mais de 2,8 milhões de veículos. Entre os modelos afetados estão o Tiguan e o Golf, da Volkswagen, e o Q3, da Audi.

O g1 procurou a Volkswagen do Brasil e a Audi para saber se os modelos vendidos no país estão incluídos no recall, mas as montadoras não responderam até a publicação desta reportagem.

Segundo a Agência Federal de Transportes Motorizados (KBA) da Alemanha, órgão semelhante à Secretaria Nacional de Trânsito (Senatran), o recall inclui os seguintes modelos da Volkswagen:

No caso da Volkswagen, o recall afeta veículos fabricados entre 24 de setembro de 2013 e 1º de julho de 2024.

Na Audi, apenas o Q3 aparece na lista da KBA. Os veículos envolvidos foram produzidos entre 31 de outubro de 2017 e 23 de maio de 2024.

Dos modelos listados, Tiguan, Golf e Golf Variant foram vendidos no Brasil durante o período de produção apontado pela KBA. O Audi Q3 também foi comercializado no país e passou a ser produzido nacionalmente em 2016, na fábrica de São José dos Pinhais (PR).

Segundo o órgão alemão, a falha está relacionada à corrosão de um parafuso, o que pode comprometer o controle da direção dos veículos. A correção consiste na substituição do parafuso defeituoso.

articles.title: Presidents Cup Friday live scores, updates: Scottie Scheffler, Sam Burns again leading U.S. team in foursomes matches at Medinah
articles.summary: The United States took a 3-2 lead over the International team after Thursday's matches in Chicago.
articles.body:
It wasn't a totally dominant start, but the United States is taking a one-point lead into the second day at Medinah Country Club.

The U.S. team jumped out to a 3-2 advantage over the International team after the opening-round four-ball session at the Presidents Cup on Thursday. They won three of the five matches on the day, including what was a tense battle between the pairing of Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns and Min Woo Lee and Sungjae Im.

Scheffler and Burns managed to take the lead on the 17th after a slow start, and nearly chipped-in from the bunker at the last, to grab the 1UP win. That marked Burns and Scheffler's first international win together.

Play continues on Friday with a series of five foursomes matches, or alternate shot matches. Scheffler and Burns will lead the way again, but will go up against Corey Conners and Nick Taylor this time.

Friday's outing will set the stage for a doubleheader on Saturday before Sunday's singles matches close it out. The first team to 15.5 points will claim the cup. If the Americans can pull it off, they will win the event for an 11th straight time.

articles.title: Presidents Cup: Wyndham Clark thinks crowds at Medinah were 'dead' in opening round, a year after the Ryder Cup fiasco
articles.summary: The Americans took an early 3-2 lead over the International team on Thursday in Chicago.
articles.body:
While very similar events on paper, the Presidents Cup is a very different event from the Ryder Cup.

Wyndham Clark felt that difference on Thursday as the U.S. team took a 3-2 lead over the international team at Medinah Country Club. It was calm in Chicago.

"It was kind of dead out there," Clark said on Thursday night. "I felt like the momentum could have been better, to be honest, because we weren't really feeling the fans, I think, as much as normal."

Based on how things went at the Ryder Cup a year ago, that may not be a bad thing.

American fans at Bethpage Black went overboard at the Ryder Cup last fall, when the Europeans rolled to a pretty commanding win over the United States. There were plenty of incidents that crossed the line, including one when a drink was launched at Rory McIlroy and his wife, Erica .

McIlroy took the brunt of the heckling, but it was across the board. He called it "unacceptable and abusive behavior."

But as Clark noted, the crowds in Chicago on Thursday were nothing like they were at the Ryder Cup in New York. It wasn't empty, but things looked and felt like any standard PGA Tour event. The fans on site were clearly cheering for the Americans, but nothing appeared to be even close to getting out of hand.

And the Presidents Cup has been a one-sided fight since its inception in the mid-1990s. The Americans are seeking an 11th straight win, and they've only lost one time in the event's history. Without European stars on the International team, it's simply not the same fight that the Ryder Cup is. Undoubtedly, that takes some steam out of the crowd.

Clark, alongside Collin Morikawa, rolled to a 3&2 win over Ryan Fox and Adam Scott in their four-ball match on Thursday. That was one of three matches the United States won to grab the early lead.

Crowds in Chicago will get bigger as the tournament goes on, especially when the weekend hits. Clark is counting on it.

"I'm saying this more as a challenge that hopefully tomorrow and the weekend the fans are out there really rooting us on, and regardless of what happens, we have the momentum," he said.

articles.title: Presidents Cup: International team bounces back, sweeps foursomes matches to take lead at Medinah as U.S. struggles
articles.summary: The International team took a dominant 7-3 lead after winning all five foursomes matches on Friday in Chicago.
articles.body:
Well, the International team bounced back.

The Americans struggled across the board on Friday at Medinah Country Club in Chicago, and will now have to enter the weekend at an event they've dominated since the beginning with plenty of work to do if they're going to retain the Presidents Cup.

The International team dominated on Friday to jump out of the early hole they found themselves in after Thursday's four-ball session. They won all five foursomes matches during the second day of play at the Presidents Cup, and now hold a 7-3 lead entering the weekend.

It was the seventh time that a team has swept a session in Presidents Cup history, and the first since the Internationals swept the foursomes session in 2024. The four-point lead also ties the largest lead the International team has held after two sessions, matching the 1998 event — the only one that the Americans have ever lost.

The U.S. team just couldn't get anything going, even with great looks from Wyndham Clark and Scottie Scheffler down the stretch. Now, over the last two Presidents Cups and Ryder Cups, the Americans are a combined 6-24-0 in foursomes matches, via Skratch's Dan Rapaport .

"They went out there and played great. They made a ton of putts," U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker said of the International team. "I feel like our guys hit a bunch of great putts and just couldn't find the bottom of the hole. "You're going to have sessions like this in these things. I feel terrible for the guys because I know they grinded out there and gave me everything they had today, and it wasn't meant to be."

"They went out there and played great. They made a ton of putts," U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker said of the International team. "I feel like our guys hit a bunch of great putts and just couldn't find the bottom of the hole.

"You're going to have sessions like this in these things. I feel terrible for the guys because I know they grinded out there and gave me everything they had today, and it wasn't meant to be."

Hideki Matsuyama and Sungjae Im had the easiest time for the Internationals. After falling behind early, the duo carded three birdies in a four-hole stretch to suddenly take a three-hole lead through six in their matchup with Russell Henley and Jacob Bridgeman. One of those birdies even came after Im sank a putt from off the green.

They cruised to an easy 3&2 win to get a point on the board for the International team.

The International team was walking in putts throughout the course, too. Adam Scott drained a deep one himself early in his match alongside Christiaan Bezuidenhout, and the pair jumped to a three-hole lead at the turn while dominating Justin Thomas and Cameron Young. Thomas and Young didn't make a single birdie all day, and just looked off with each other throughout the round. Scott and Bezuidenhout won 3&2.

Then Ryan Fox walked one in too on the seventh with Min Woo Lee. Fox's birdie gave the International team the lead in four of the five matches at the time in a stunningly dominant start.

Si Woo Kim and Tom Kim erupted on the ninth green after a deep putt of their own, which gave them a two-shot lead at the turn over Patrick Cantlay and Xander Schauffele. They ended up taking a 4&3 win.

Scheffler and Sam Burns, who picked up their first international match play win together on Thursday, struggled to get past Corey Conners and Nick Taylor in the first group of the day. Scheffler had two great looks down the stretch to tie the match back up, and even had a golden opportunity at the 18th after Taylor sent his drive way off to the right of the fairway.

But Taylor stuck his approach to 2 feet after Conners pitched it out from behind the trees to save par, which sealed their 1-up win.

"It was more so redemption for that tee shot, but happy to walk away with a 4, and fortunate there that Sam's lipped out," Taylor said.

The only real bright side for the Americans came from Clark and Morikawa. Clark carried his pairing on Thursday to a win, and Morikawa managed five birdies together to keep pace with Fox and Lee. But Fox kept putting lights out, and walked in another long birdie at the 16th to put them back on top and eventually seal the 1-up win. That completed the five-match sweep, and gave the International team a four-point lead entering the weekend.

There is still a long way to go at Medinah. Saturday will feature a doubleheader with four-ball matches in the morning and foursomes matches in the afternoon before all 24 golfers will square off in singles matches on Sunday. But for now, the Americans have to make a significant move if they want to avoid being the first U.S. group to lose the cup in nearly two decades.

"This thing is 35, 40 percent over. It's not even halftime of a football game," Snedeker said. "There's a lot of golf left. … I'm fortunate to have these guys in the team room because I know what they're made of. I know what they're built of. It's going to be a long weekend, a lot of golf still left to play."

articles.summary: The United States team ran into some trouble during the second day of the 2026 Presidents Cup at Medinah Country Club in Illinois.
articles.body:
The United States team ran into some trouble during the second day of the 2026 Presidents Cup at Medinah Country Club in Illinois.

After the U.S. squad held a 3-2 lead over the International team following Thursday's four-ball play, the Internationals dominated Friday's foursome matches to take a 7-3 advantage.

Scheffler and Burns held an early lead over Conners and Taylor in the opening match of the day, but the International duo eventually jumped in front with a birdie on hole No. 6.

While the U.S. team later tied the match, Conners and Taylor took another lead on No. 12. Burns eventually missed a birdie putt on No. 18 for the tie, giving the International team a full point.

Matsuyama and Im also fell into an early deficit against Henley and Bridgeman, but moved in front by carding three birdies across four holes from No. 3 through No. 6.

The Americans were unable to recover, as the International team easily took the second match.

The third match of the day was a hard-fought contest, as both duos were tied through five holes.

Fox and Lee eventually took the first lead with a birdie on No. 6, but Clark and Morikawa finally grabbed a lead of their own on No. 12.

Clutch putting from Fox and Lee put the Internationals back in front and gave them a full point, though.

Thomas and Young struggled to start their foursome match against Scott and Bezuidenhout, picking up a bogey on the first hole.

As for the International duo, they ended the match with five birdies compared to just one for the U.S. pair. Scott played his 56th Presidents Cup match, setting a new record.

Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim ended the day with a dominant showing against Cantlay and Schauffele, as they never trailed at any point during the match before it ended after hole No. 15.

The International team is attempting to win the Presidents Cup for the first time since 1998.

Saturday will feature both foursome matches and four-ball play.

articles.title: Presidents Cup: International Team stun Team USA with session sweep in Friday foursomes to build shock lead at Medinah
articles.summary: The International Team take a four-point lead into the weekend at Medinah after winning all five matches in Friday's foursomes session against Team USAwatch day three live on Saturday from 1pm on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
The United States have never been beaten on home soil in the biennial contest and have won 13 of the previous 15 editions, although now find themselves behind after an impressive Friday performance from Geoff Ogilvy's International Team at Medinah.

Canadian duo Corey Conners and Nick Taylor held off world No 1 Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns to claim a 1up win in the top match, having already seen Hideki Matsuyama and Sungjae Im despatch Russell Henley and Jacob Bridgeman 3&2.

Open champion Ryan Fox partnered Min Woo Lee to a final-hole win over Collin Morikawa and Wyndham Clark, before Christiaan Bezuidenhout and Adam Scott wrapped up a 3&2 win over Justin Thomas and Wyndham Clark.

Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim then claimed their second win as many days with a 4&3 win over Patrick Cantlay and Xander Schauffele, the second successive Presidents Cup that the International Team have swept the Friday foursomes.

The dramatic turnaround sees the Internationals bounce back from losing Thursday's fourballs session 3-2 and gives them a four-point advantage heading into the weekend, leaving them needing 8.5 points from the 20 left on offer to claim a first win since 1998.

How Internationals built shock lead at Medinah

Scheffler has now lost eight of his nine foursomes matches for Team USA in Presidents Cups or Ryder Cups, despite giving him and Burns the early lead after a sensational approach into the second set up a birdie.

Burns went out of bounds to lose the next hole before the Internationals responded to losing the fourth hole by winning the next two, with Conners and Taylor never relinquishing control to keep the pair one up with one to play.

Conners had to pitch out from thick rough before Taylor fired a stunning approach from the fairway to a foot, securing the par, with Burns lipping out with his 20-foot birdie try to tie the match.

"We just tried to be relentless out there," Conners said. "Both hit a lot of quality shots and Nick [Taylor] made some key putts there towards the end to keep us in the position. His approach shot into the last here was unbelievable!"

Matsuyama partnered Ryo Hisatsune to victory on the opening day but formed a formidable partnership with Im, as the pair won four consecutive holes from the third to race into a 3up lead against Henley and Bridgeman.

The American won successive holes from the 10th but Matsuyama nailed a 20-foot birdie to win the 12th and Im won the 15th, before the Internationals closed out the point when Matsuyama rattled an unlikely par at the par-three 16th.

Hopes of a session sweep increased when Fox posted successive birdies from the 15th to flip his and Lee's match, with Morikawa missing a five-foot putt to level at the 17th and allowing the Internationals to close out another point with a par at the last.

Thomas and Young never led during their match against Scott - playing in a record-breaking 56th Presidents Cup match - and Bezuidenhout, who wrapped up an impressive win with a 30-foot birdie on the 16th.

"There's a lot of golf left," Scott insisted. "Tomorrow is a big day. I think we had a similar situation two years ago in Canada [2024 Presidents Cup]. Hopefully we learned from that and we can back a great day up tomorrow."

Kim and Kim also had control in the bottom match, posting six birdies in alternate shot, with Team USA's pointless session confirmed when Schauffele missed from three feet to extend that match at the 15th.

Ogilvy savours 'incredible' day for Internationals

International Team captain Geoff Ogilvy :

"We loved how we played yesterday - the first match could have gone either way and it ended up 2-3 their way, but we just wanted to come win this session.

"They [Internationals] were all in a really good frame of mind, but you would never imagine doing five sets. We did it in Montreal [sweep], so maybe it's a pattern now. We never mentioned that, but the boys played really well. It was an incredible day for us."

"Hats off to the International Team - they went out there and played great. They made a ton of putts. I feel like our guys hit a bunch of great putts and just couldn't find the bottom of the hole.

"You're going to have sessions like this in these things. I feel terrible for the guys because I know they grinded out there and gave me everything they had today, and it wasn't meant to be. That being said, there's still 20 points out there. There's a lot of golf left to play."

articles.title: The Packers offensive line is broken, how did we get here?
articles.summary: Green Bay's disastrous offensive line performance is the result of a series of unfortunate events and mistakes from the top of the organization down.
articles.body:
For more than a decade, the Green Bay Packers offensive line was one the strongest pillars of what drove their success. Now, it is completely broken.

As late as 2024, the Packers were PFF's third highest graded pass-blocking unit. After three games in 2026 they are 32nd by a distance with an embarrassing 41.7 grade. Since 2006, no team has ever graded lower than 43.4 across an entire season.

The truth is it is not just one thing, but a series of unfortunate events and mistakes, with plenty of blame to be shared, much of it difficult to correctly assign.

For the sake of this discussion, let's focus on pass blocking, as that has always been Green Bay 's bread and butter more so than run blocking.

In 2024, Green Bay had three players with a PFF pass block grade of 80 or higher: Elgton Jenkins , Zach Bako-Bewele and Rasheed Walker . Sean Rhyan and Josh Myers had grades of 65.6 and 63.9 respectively, and first-round rookie Jordan Morgan wasn't even required to start.

There were personnel differences in 2025, as Myers, their worst starter from the year before, left in free agency, with the Packers deciding to move Jenkins to center and signing Aaron Banks to a four-year, $77 million contract to play guard. They also drafted Anthony Belton in the second round.

It was not a huge amount of change, yet their collective ranking fell all the way to 22nd. Walker fell off a cliff, Jenkins' transition to center did not go as well as the Packers hoped, Banks was arguably no better than Myers, and most notably, injuries played a big factor.

Jenkins went down midseason, while Banks and Bako-Bewele were banged up all year. Mostly due to these injury issues, it was reasonable to think 2025 was a blip.

Instead, the O-line has been far worse in the early stages of this season, and it is hard to divorce the many contributing factors from one another. Let's explore the possible explanations.

Offensive line coach Luke Butkus has drawn a lot of criticism, with plenty of fans wanting him fired at the end of last year. By extension, head coach Matt LaFleur and offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich have been under fire as well.

Green Bay's failures in the basics of executing their assignment or blocking who they are supposed to certainly do not reflect well on coaching.

It cannot be that simple though, and the idea that the Packers offensive line instantly declined once he was promoted from his assistant role is not backed up by the facts. In his first three years as the O-line coach from 2022 to 2024, they ranked third, 10th and third in PFF's pass block grades.

Stenavich was the previous coach and did an excellent job before moving up to offensive coordinator, is still on the staff and likely has a big role with the O-line to this day. It is hard to believe Stenavich and Butkus both simply forgot how to coach.

Attention then turns to general manager Brian Gutekunst, who has certainly had some missteps. Whatever the problem may be, it is not a case of him failing to invest enough in the offensive line.

Entering training camp, the presumed starters were a first-round pick in Morgan, a $77 million free agent signing in Banks, a third rounder on a second contract in Rhyan, a second-round pick in Belton and a highly-paid second-contract player in Bako-Bewele.

He has been criticised for not being more aggressive in trying to improve the O-line this offseason, but from his perspective, it is understandable that he would look at the coaching staff and say: "I've spent the resources. Over to you."

Is the problem that he simply made bets on the wrong players? There is certainly more validity to that argument.

In signing Banks, he made the common but problematic free agency mistake of handing an elite contract to a non-elite player.

Belton was a curious pick in the second round when it was made, and perhaps one of Gutekunst's bigger errors was assuming Belton, Jacob Monk and Jager Burton was enough competition for what was supposed to be just one available guard spot entering camp.

Admittedly, he probably did not imagine all three having to start by Week 3, with Belton back at tackle where it seemed his future did not lie a few months ago, but none of the three look close to good enough.

Going back to 2025, Gutekunst has to take some of the blame for the failed Jenkins experiment at center. At the time though, few people on the outside were criticizing the decision to move him back to his college position, and he is now playing center again for the Browns .

There is similar revisionism happening with Rasheed Walker as he looks solid for the Panthers , yet no one disagreed with the decision to let him go at the end of last season, especially coming off a poor campaign, and Morgan seems to be finding his feet week by week.

Is it fair to have expected Morgan to be better than Walker out of the gate in his first season starting at left tackle? Surely his two-year ramp up period was designed to cut out some of these teething problems, but then again, he did not play left tackle during that time.

That last part speaks to another criticism during the O-line struggles. Has the Packers' cross-training of their players and penchant for moving them around gone too far? Potentially, but again, that strategy worked just fine before 2025.

Perhaps the most underdiscussed potential problem with the current group could be a lack of experience on the actual line itself, not just individually, but in terms of banked reps together, especially with Bako-Bewele and Banks out injured.

That is not necessarily an excuse though. In this instance, it is potentially an indictment of the organization's steadfast belief in their ability to develop linemen, plug anyone into the lineup or set up and effectively implement succession plans, and not recognizing the importance of experience.

Look at the Chicago Bears after Ben Johnson arrived as head coach. They spent endless resources finding sure things on the O-line, even if that meant trading draft picks for high-priced veterans like Joe Thuney and Jonah Jackson .

The Browns just rebuilt their entire offensive line in one offseason, mostly with vets like former Packer Jenkins. After finishing 32nd in PFF's pass block grading last year, they are fifth early in 2026.

Fans are looking for the smoking gun, but for the Packers to be this bad on the offensive line, it cannot be just one person's fault. It is a collective problem, and that means right now, making a personnel change or firing someone is unlikely to change anything.

That is not comforting news, as it means no one really knows if this can be fixed, or how. Doing so this season will be very difficult, although surely they can play better than the truly disastrous performances from the first few weeks.

Beyond 2026, it will be incumbent on the front office and the coaching staff to dig deep into what has gone wrong and commit wholeheartedly to finding solutions moving forward, because this year's O-line is threatening to sink the season before it can even get going.

articles.title: Presidents Cup: International team fight back from 3-2 down to take 7-3 lead over USA
articles.summary: The International team produce a brilliant fightback in the foursomes on day two of the Presidents Cup to take a 7-3 lead over the United States.
articles.body:
The International team produced a brilliant fightback in the foursomes on day two of the Presidents Cup to take a 7-3 lead over the United States.

The US had been 3-2 up after the fourballs on Thursday but in a stunning turnaround were beaten in all five matches in the alternate-shot format in Medinah on Friday.

It boosted their hopes of a first victory in the event since 1998 and only a second since the competition began in 1994.

Geoff Ogilvy's side secured their first point of the day as Sungjae Im and Hideki Matsuyama saw off Russell Henley and Jacob Bridgeman 3&2.

Canadian duo Corey Conners and Nick Taylor then produced a stunning result as they held on to beat world number one Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns by one hole.

Burns almost snatched a half when his 20-foot putt at the last lipped out.

Open champion Ryan Fox and Min Woo Lee also edged a see-saw contest with Collin Morikawa and Wyndham Clark by one hole, before Adam Scott and Christiaan Bezuidenhout defeated Justin Thomas and Cameron Young 3&2.

Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim wrapped up the day with a dominant 4&3 victory over Patrick Cantlay and Xander Schauffele.

There will be four further foursomes matches and four more fourballs on Saturday, with 12 singles games taking place on Sunday.

articles.title: LPGA Tour: England's Charley Hull overcomes post-Solheim Cup illness to close on early lead at NW Arkansas Championship
articles.summary: Yuna Nishimura leads Yu Liu after the opening round of the Walmart NW Arkansas Championship; England's Charley Hull and Lottie Woad both sit in early LPGA Tour contention; watch the second round live on Saturday from 9pm on Sky Sports+
articles.body:
Hull, making her first start since featuring in Team Europe's Solheim Cup win in the Netherlands earlier this month, mixed seven birdies with one bogey during her opening-round 65 at Pinnacle Country Club.

The Englishwoman, who revealed post-round she had tonsillitis during Europe's 15-13 victory over the United States, sits in tied-third on six under as Japan's Yuna Nishimura set the early pace.

Hull failed to take advantage of two of the three par fives but responded well to being over-par early in her round, posting three birdies in a five-hole stretch from the 13th before adding four more in a six-hole burst after the turn.

"I felt like I played pretty solid," Hull said. "It was quite weird, last week at home I didn't hit a golf ball for like five days because I was bed-bound and I was so poorly.

"After the Solheim Cup I had the flu, I had sickness and everything. I nearly pulled out of this week because I felt like I wasn't prepared enough! I came over to America on Saturday, had sponsor stuff up until Tuesday and got in here late Tuesday night.

"It wasn't really the best prep, but actually I come in here with no expectations. I felt like I hit it pretty well tee-to-green and putted decent."

A final-hole eagle pushed Nishimura into a one-shot advantage over China's Yu Liu, who held the initial clubhouse lead after a bogey-free 64, while Hull is joined in the logjam on six under by Solheim Cup teammate Celine Boutier.

England's Jodi Ewart Shadoff threatened a late run at the lead until two bogeys in her last three holes saw her post a five-under 66, with compatriots Lottie Woad and Caley McGinty also three back.

"With it only being three rounds, you want to get off to a good to start and try and not drop too many shots," Woad explained. "If you hit a lot of greens like I did today then you're not going to make too many bogeys."

Mimi Rhodes opened with a four-under 67 and Chiara Tamburlini - who narrowly missed out on Solheim Cup qualification - also lies four behind after a low-scoring opening day.

articles.title: IIT-M & Unicorn India hit ₹450 cr first close for its fund; Backs 4 deep-tech startups
articles.summary: IIT Madras Research Park and Unicorn India Ventures hit ₹450 crore first close for a ₹1,000 crore deep-tech fund, backing 4 startups; final close by 2027.
articles.body: Chennai: IIT Madras Research Park (IITMRP) and deep-tech-focused venture capital firm Unicorn India Ventures announced the first close of its fund at Rs 450 crore. It has also backed four deep-tech startups. articles.title: From watching others win to owning the moment: Khalin Joshi claims Bengaluru Open in five-shot romp
articles.summary: BENGALURU: For years, the Karnataka Golf Association had been a stage where Khalin Joshi had watched others have their moment.
articles.body: BENGALURU: For years, the Karnataka Golf Association had been a stage where Khalin Joshi had watched others have their moment. On Friday, finally, it was his turn.The 34-year-old Bengaluru golfer completed a wire-to-wire victory at the Bengaluru Open, closing with a two-under 70 to turn a three-shot overnight lead into a commanding five-stroke triumph. More than the 10th PGTI title of his career, it was the win Joshi had quietly longed for — a title on his home turf, in front of his people.“I have no words. It’s just something I’ve always dreamt of doing,” Joshi said after signing off with a 20-under-268 (61-68-69-70).The victory was his second in as many weeks, following last week’s Raipur Open, and his fourth of the season. It also capped a remarkable turnaround for a golfer who had not won on the PGTI since 2022.The numbers tell the story of a player who has found another gear in the second half of the season. Joshi’s latest victory was his third in about six starts, while his wins in Srinagar in Aug and Bengaluru this week both came wire-to-wire. He has now led from start to finish in three tournaments this season.“I’m having a dream run. I’ve been playing really well. I’ve been working on my mind a lot, so I’m happy that some results are finally showing up,” he said.But Joshi insists there has been no dramatic overhaul of his game. Instead, the biggest change has been in his mindset. “I’m just trying to be more present on the golf course. Apart from that, I keep working on my swing, keep working on my game,” he said.Joshi has also been working with Thailand-based English coach Richard Spence for the past one-and-a-half years, focusing on simple fundamentals — alignment, ball position, grip, posture and keeping his swing on plane.But the bigger battle, he admits, has been with his mind. “My mind usually keeps racing, so I think I make mental errors which causes bogeys and causes me to lose tournaments,” he said. “Now I think that my mind is getting a little stronger and I know deep down that if I’m doing my best, I’m hard to beat.”That belief was tested on Friday. Joshi admitted to feeling nervous at the start, but a 35-footer for birdie on the opening hole settled him. Two bogeys in the middle of the round could have opened the door for the chasing pack.Instead, Joshi stayed aggressive. “I knew that I had a comfortable lead. Just had to keep staying aggressive,” added Joshi, who had his girlfriend on the bag for the first time in a DP World PGTI event. She had previously caddied for him on the Asian Development Tour and Asian Tour.It was a mindset that has transformed a player who felt he had often failed to close tournaments despite possessing the game to win them.At KGA, there was no repeat of those old doubts. Joshi stayed in the moment, hit the shots he needed and walked away with the home title he had been chasing for years.“I’ve seen so many of the Bangalore boys, so many of the other players coming and just snatching the tournament from me like last minute,” he said. “It’s been difficult over the years. articles.title: Open de France: England's Matt Fitzpatrick takes five-shot lead into final day as Tommy Fleetwood withdraws with illness
articles.summary: Matt Fitzpatrick heads into the final day on 19 under and five clear of France's Tom Vaillant; Fitzpatrick has carded just one bogey over the first three days at Le Golf National; watch the final round live on Sunday from 11.30am on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
The Englishman held a one-shot advantage heading into the weekend at Le Golf National but pulled further ahead with a six-under 65 on Saturday afternoon, mixing seven birdies with his first bogey of the week.

Fitzpatrick - already a winner on the PGA Tour at the Valspar Championship, RBC Heritage and Zurich Classic of New Orleans this year - moved to 19 under and with a commanding advantage over France's Tom Vaillant.

Spain's Eugenio Chacarra, third in the Race to Dubai standings behind Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy, charged into a share of third after carding an eagle and seven birdies in a round-of-the-week 62.

Ryder Cup hopeful Kristoffer Reitan, Brandon Stone, Angel Hidalgo and Jeff Winther are also in the group six behind, while England's Tommy Fleetwood withdrew ahead of the third round due to illness.

How Fitzpatrick extended his lead in France

Fitzpatrick quickly grabbed control by birdieing the first and two-putting from 40 feet to take advantage of the par-five third, with the former US Open champion adding another birdie at the sixth.

He failed to get up and down to save par from off the par-three eighth green but responded by birdieing the par-five next, then added three more after the turn - including from tap-in range at the par-four 13th - to pull further clear.

"Just another really, really solid day," Fitzpatrick said. "I felt really comfortable out there. It's always nice to get off to a nice start like that and then you can kind of kick on from there.

"I felt like that my game was pretty solid all day. I feel like I'm in a position that if I go and shoot a good round tomorrow, then obviously it makes it almost impossible to catch. But a long way to go and just take it hole by hole."

Vaillant will play alongside Fitzpatrick in the final group after carding five birdies and a bogey during a third-round 67, while Chacarra's 62 included a 25-foot eagle at the ninth and five birdies in a seven-hole stretch on the back nine.

"I've been playing unbelievable golf the first couple rounds," Chacarra explained. "The putts didn't want to go in and today we finally see some putts go in. So happy with a good moving day."

Winther stumbled with a double-bogey at the par-five 14th in his third-round 70, dropping him back to 13 under, while first-round leader Michael Kim slipped a further shot back after finishing his day with a double-bogey at the par-four last.

English duo Sam Bairstow and Joe Dean carded matching 66s to head into the final day on 11 under, while Fleetwood was due to head into the weekend on six under before his withdrawal.

articles.title: Baramati among eight tehsils in Pune district in state’s list
articles.summary: Pune district: Baramati and seven other tehsils declared drought-affected after 25%+ rainfall deficit and 21-day dry spell; crops hit, assessment planned.
articles.body: Pune: Baramati, Indapur, Daund, Shirur, Purandar and the usually rain-sufficient Khed, Velhe and Bhor are among the eight tehsils in Pune district declared as drought-affected after rainfall deficit in these areas exceeded 25% and dry spells lasted at least 21 days.The district’s uneven rainfall pattern means the western and eastern regions face different agricultural challenges, with Shirur, Daund, Indapur and Baramati forming part of its relatively dry belt.“We have lost almost half of our crop because it did not rain in Aug-Sept,” Purandar farmer Vitthal Zende said. The prolonged dry spell has turned a productive green pea harvest into a season of heavy losses.Onion cultivation has been severely affected in Shirur and Daund as water sources are dry in Sept, while vegetable growers in Purandar who supply to Pune’s markets are facing difficulties.Pune district agriculture officer Vaibhav Tambe told TOI, “We are planning to execute a ground-truthing exercise in the affected tehsils immediately to understand the actual crop loss.”Several affected tehsils are important horticultural and vegetable-producing centres. Indapur, known for its export-quality pomegranates, has reported stress in plantations after the rainfall gap, a senior agriculture officer said.Pomegranates, figs, custard apples and bananas grown in these regions are supplied to domestic markets and exported to Gulf countries, Southeast Asia and European markets.In Velhe and Bhor, traditionally among the high rainfall areas and known for paddy cultivation, the situation is grim. “Many paddy cultivators could not fertilize their crops and have reported diseases. The overall harvest will reduce significantly this season,” an agriculture officer said.Kharif crops have been severely affected in the tehsils while cash crops, mainly sugar cane, is in a good state because of canal and river water. But in some villages in Shirur water sources are limited and they have dried up in the last two weeks,” officials said.Activist Shantaram Saravade from Khed tehsil said the ground assessment is crucial to determine the extent of damage and based on these reports, farmers will get help from the state govt. “Some pockets in these eight tehsils are better off. articles.title: This Packers rookie has a message for fans after team's disastrous start
articles.summary: Packers rookie linebacker Dani Dennis-Sutton gave a four-worded message on X to fans a day after the team's disastrous home opener.
articles.body:
It's been less than two weeks and only 13 days since the Green Bay Packers ' 2026 season kicked off, but after three games many fans likely feel that the season is over.

There has been a collapse, there's been one of the worst home losses in years , there's been brutal injuries, there's a team that can't protect its quarterback , run the ball and one that has been undisciplined.

The Packers look to be a team in crisis without a path forward from their current state. All their weaknesses were on display during a 21-point loss in their home opener on "Thursday Night Football" to the Atlanta Falcons . And fans let them know how they felt as they booed the team early and often.

If that was a one-off fans might overlook it. But it's been a pattern that goes beyond the Falcons game. The Packers are 1-7 in their last eight games overall, dating to last season.

But a Packers rookie is speaking up or at least he wants Packers Nation to know what he's feeling.

"This s--- ain't over," linebacker Dani Dennis-Sutton wrote on X on Friday, Sept. 25, a day after the Packers were run off the field by the Falcons .

It's true plenty of games have to be played in the 2026 season, 14 to be exact.

And the last time the Packers were 1-2 it was in 2014 when they were one special teams blunder from going to the Super Bowl.

After losing its second game in Week 3, Aaron Rodgers then told everyone to R-E-L-A-X.

That team would win four straight and nine of 10 games as the Packers went on to finish 12-4, win the NFC North division, earn a playoff bye, beat the Dallas Cowboys in the divisional round before losing to the Seattle Seahawks in the NFC Championship Game after collapsing late.

Could the 2026 Packers make a similar comeback?

Like in 2014, the Packers played and defeated the New York Jets in Week 2 and followed it with a poor offensive showing the next. But 12 years later, if this team can't find a solution at offensive line or running back or begin to tackle they won't follow what that 2014 team did no matter how many games are remaining.

The Packers picked Dennis-Sutton, 22, with the 120th overall pick in the fourth round.

Through three games, he has nine tackles (two solo and seven assisted). Dennis-Sutton had a half a sack in the Week 2 overtime win at the New York Jets and had two assisted tackles on Thursday night.

His optimism may fuel from the fact that the Packers are getting his mentor, Micah Parsons , back in the coming weeks.

Dennis-Sutton and Parsons both starred at Penn State.

The All-Pro edge rusher Parsons hasn't played since tearing his ACL during the Packers' Week 15 game against the Denver Broncos last season. A return date could come in mid-October.

Parsons has been on the sidelines this season giving his defensive teammates motivation. The defense performed well against the Jets in helping save that game but they were exposed by one of the best running backs in the game four days later.

Bijan Robinson rushed for 194 yards and two touchdowns, reminiscent of when Derrick Henry put up 216 yards and four touchdowns against the Green Bay defense in the Packers' home finale during the 2025 season.

articles.title: Packers Urged to Make Major Offensive Line Shakeup
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers need to find something to do on the offensive line to shake things up. With all of the injuries and players struggling, the team does n...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers need to find something to do on the offensive line to shake things up. With all of the injuries and players struggling, the team does not have many strong options. However, Justis Mosqueda of Acme Packing Company is a potential option that has not been looked at yet.

Mosqueda argues the team should start Jager Burton at left guard, Anthony Belton at right guard, and then either John Williams or Travis Glover playing right tackle.

Mosqueda noted that Belton struggled at guard; however, his tape would look fine had he been playing guard.

"Anthony Belton is still a people mover, but he can't hang in pass protection at tackle when he's going against wider edges who build up steam before the point of contact," added Mosqueda. "He's a guard playing tackle. The coaching staff needs to fix this."

Mosqueda suggests starting one of their backup tackles at right tackle in place of Belton.

Green Bay Packers Should Shuffle Offensive Line

Williams is a former seventh-round pick from the 2025 NFL Draft. Unfortunately, he was injured during his rookie season and did not even play in the preseason. In 2026, he played in all three preseason games, but was at left tackle.

So, the Packers switching him to right tackle with little experience for his first career start might be unlikely.

Glover is a 2024 sixth-round pick. He had nine snaps at right tackle as a rookie and has 147 snaps at right tackle in the preseason throughout his career. This year, he had 38 snaps on the right side.

So, if they are going to go through with the plan, it would likely be Glover on the right side with Belton.

They might not be as strong at right tackle, but they are much improved at right guard.

Packers Urged to Keep Jager Burton at Left Guard

Mosqueda added that the team needs to keep Burton at left guard as well. Green Bay has played Donovan Jennings and Aaron Banks at left guard ahead of Burton. However, both got hurt, and the team had to throw in the fifth-round rookie.

Mosqueda notes that even with right guard Jacob Monk being moved out of the right guard spot, he should not replace Burton.

"Jager Burton played poorly, but he doesn't look physically overmatched like Jacob Monk. Monk is a backup center playing starting guard. This cannot continue. I don't care how nice of a guy he is in the locker room," Mosqueda added.

Jennings started in Week 1 and struggled. The team tried to start Banks in Week 2, but he hurt his toe. So, the team put Jennings in, but he got hurt. Burton was the third option, but he played the best. Then, he held down the spot again in Week 3. It was not perfect, but in the name of continuity, he is becoming a likely option.

The only question would be what the team does if starting Sean Rhyan misses time with his hand injury or if Banks returns. For now, there is no harm in trying this option.

"The Packers have lost two of their first three games this season by 17+ points. They had not lost multiple games by 17+ points in an entire season since 2017," wrote the NFL analyst in his post on X (formerly Twitter).

The Packers opened the season with a 17-point defeat to Minnesota after allowing 22 unanswered points in the fourth quarter. However, Thursday night brought an even more damaging result, as Green Bay fell by 21 points in what was easily its worst showing of the season.

The Packers have also lost several contributors to injuries, with Jayden Reed , Zach Bako Bewele, and Aaron Banks among those dealing with setbacks. Even with those challenges in mind, Green Bay's performances have fallen short of the standard the organization normally expects.

Thursday's loss was certainly a setback, but it has not put the Packers out of contention. A quick turnaround would give the team enough time to recover from its difficult opening stretch and make a push later in the season. articles.body:
The United States will need to come back in singles on Sunday to avoid losing the Presidents Cup for the first time since 1998.

The International team lost some ground in Saturday but will carry a 10.5-7.5 lead into Sunday's final round of competition.

Here is a look at results and highlights from the latest two rounds of competition at Medinah Country Club.

The international team, which entered Saturday with a 7-3 lead, trailed in all four-ball matches before completing two comebacks.

Jackson Koivun made some highlight-reel shots, but he and Justin Thomas were unable to hold onto an early lead as Min Woo Lee and Sunjae Im tied their four-ball match on No. 16.

The next U.S. team to lose an early lead was Collin Morikawa and Wyndham Clark, who went 2-up through eight holes before Si Woo Kim converted consecutive birdies on Nos. 16 and 17.

Chris Gotterup and Cameron Young started to turn things around for the United States by securing a full point in their matchup against Corey Conners and Nick Taylor.

Scottie Scheffler impressed with a tying birdie putt on No. 15 before Sam Burns made a birdie of own to secure the United States' second full-point win of the day.

Scheffler rested for the afternoon as the international team headed into foursomes with an 8.5-5.5 lead.

The United States started to chip away at the international lead thanks to victories from Young and Gotterup as well as Patrick Cantlay and Xander Schauffele. The latter duo dealt Si Woo Kim and Tom Kim their first defeat of the tournament.

Ryan Fox and Min Woo Lee helped the international team recover some of the advantage with consecutive birdies down the back nine of a victory over Burns and Clark.

The United States' Russell Henley and Jacob Bridgeman were 3-up after No. 10 but fell short of closing out a win against Nick Taylor and Corey Conners.

The Presidents Cup concludes Sunday with 12 singles matches. U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker will announce who will be representing the United States in the final round later Saturday.

articles.title: Presidents Cup: International Team take historic 10.5-7.5 lead over Team USA into Sunday singles and chase Medinah win
articles.summary: A tied afternoon foursomes sessions gave the International Team a three-point lead into the final day at Medinah; Internationals need five points from the Sunday singles to claim just their second Presidents Cup win ever; watch the Sunday singles live from 4.30pm on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Geoff Ogilvy's side held a four-point advantage after the first two days at Medinah Country Club, following their historic foursomes sessions sweep on Friday, then added 1.5 points from four matches during a tight Saturday fourballs session.

Team USA captain Brandt Snedeker benched world No 1 Scottie Scheffler for the afternoon foursomes, where they threatened their own session sweep after grabbing the early lead in all four matches.

Cameron Young and Chris Gotterup thrashed Adam Scott and Sungjae Im 6&4, before Patrick Cantlay and Xander Schauffele saw off Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim 2&1 to reduce the deficit further, only for the Internationals to fight back in an impressive finish.

Ryan Fox and Min Woo Lee bounced back from falling behind early to defeat Sam Burns and Wyndham Clark 3&2 in the bottom match, guaranteeing the Internationals would start the Sunday singles ahead for just the fourth time ever.

Their shock lead then increased further via Canadian duo Corey Conners and Nick Taylor, who recovered from losing their first three holes and being three down with eight to play to beat Russell Henley and Jacob Bridgeman 1up.

A shared foursomes session leaves the Internationals with a glorious opportunity to end their run of 10 consecutive Presidents Cup defeats and claim a famous victory, which would be their first since 1998 and just their second in the event's history.

The International Team require five more points from the 12 singles matches to complete their unlikely success, while Team USA need 7.5 points on the final day to avoid an embarrassing home upset or eight points for a comeback victory.

Snedeker reveals 'mistakes' as Internationals 'weathered the storm'

"I thought our guys battled hard. It was a tough day out there. This golf course got really tough this afternoon. There's such a fine line between good shots and bad shots and I was proud of the way the guys hung in there and battled.

"I challenged the guys this afternoon to go out there and be that team that we need them to be and got Scottie (Scheffler) some much-needed rest, so he can go out there tomorrow and be the Scheffler that we know he is.

" It's going to be a long, hard day tomorrow. I've got the right guys in that team room. They're going to compete. So proud of how they've kind of hung in there this week, despite all of my mistakes. Can't wait to see them go out there tomorrow and compete."

International Team captain Geoff Ogilvy :

"What a day! They (Team USA) came out firing, as we knew they would. They were up in all four in the morning and we thought we stole a point and a half a little bit, to get out of that with only 2.5-1.5.

"This afternoon, same thing. The United States came out playing well, which we know they're going to. They're some of the best players in the world, but the boys hung tough and sort of weathered the storm if you like and started making a few putts.

"It's tough when there's all red on the board, but to get 2-2 out of that afternoon session and to go into tomorrow with a lead, which was the goal at the start of the week, I'm very proud of them."

Min Woo Lee and Im recovered from being two down with four to play to tie the top match against American duo Jackson Koivun and Justin Thomas, who said post-match that he felt like he 'let down' his rookie team-mate.

The Internationals had already extended their overnight lead when Kim and Kim recovered from being two down after eight holes to beat Collin Morikawa and Clark 2&1, shushing the crowd in celebration, only for Team USA to claim the other two matches.

Gotterup and Young won the first four holes against Taylor and Conners before the Canadians halved their lead around the turn, but Gotterup nailed three huge birdies - of 30 feet of longer - from the 13th to complete a 2&1 win.

Hideki Matsuyama and Ryo Hisatsune came from one down to move one ahead in the bottom match, only for Scheffler to nail a 20-foot birdie at the 15th and flip momentum. Scheffler then watched on as Burns claimed back-to-back holes to close a 2&1 win, cutting the International Team's overnight lead.

"The hole felt small for a while, but it opened up there on 15," Scheffler said. "It was an important one there, because Ryo [Hisatsune] was on basically the same line as me. It was nice to be able to hole that one and put some pressure on them."

articles.title: President's Cup: Internationals hold three-point lead after resisting United States fightback
articles.summary: The Internationals team could secure a first President's Cup in 28 years on Sunday after holding off a United States fightback on day three in Medinah.
articles.body:
The International team need five points on the final day to secure a first Presidents Cup in 28 years after holding off a United States fightback on day three in Medinah.

The Internationals were behind in every match at one stage but will go into Sunday's singles holding a 10-5-7.5 lead.

The hosts had the better of the morning session, winning two and tying one of the four-balls.

But the teams split the afternoon foursomes, with Canada's Corey Conners saving par at the 18th to win the final match on the course and preserve the Internationals' three-point lead.

The International team have only won the President's Cup once since its inception in 1994 and never on American soil.

"We were down in every match, and to come back and get one and a half points out of this morning, we felt that was a little victory because we were down everywhere," said team captain Geoff Ogilvy.

"This afternoon, the same thing happened. Team USA played so well all day. They played some really high-level foursomes, especially this afternoon.

"For the boys to somehow come back and pinch two points out of that and split the session was amazing."

Sunday sees 12 singles games take place, with each side needing 15.5 points to seal victory.

articles.title: LPGA Tour: Lauren Coughlin makes history with nine consecutive birdies and front-nine 26 at Walmart NW Arkansas Championship
articles.summary: Yuna Nishimura takes a five-shot lead into the final day at the Walmart NW Arkansas Championship; Lauren Coughlin fired nine consecutive birdies and made LPGA Tour history during her second-round 61; watch the final round live on Sunday from 7pm on Sky Sports+
articles.body:
Coughlin became the first player ever on the LPGA Tour to open a round with nine consecutive birdies, seeing her race to the turn in 26 at Pinnacle Country Club and card the lowest nine-hole total ever on the circuit.

The American - who started her second round on the back nine - ended her streak with a par at the first and then failed to take advantage of the par-five next, only to birdie the par-three third and raise hopes of the first '59 round' on the LPGA Tour since 2001.

Annika Sorenstam's record remains safe after Coughlin closed her 10-under 61 with six consecutive pars, lifting her to eight under and eight shots behind leader Yuna Nishimura in Arkansas.

"I was making a lot of those mid-range putts," Coughlin explained. "I hit everything pretty much inside 12 feet on my whole front nine. My longest putt might've been the 17th, which was probably about 15 feet or so.

"Other than that, everything just seemed to be going exactly how far I wanted it to, right at the hole and I was putting really good putts on them. Couldn't quite get it close enough (to a '59 round') unfortunately those last few holes."

Nishimura carded a second successive 63 to move to 16 under and take a five-shot lead into the final day over Auston Kim, Mary Liu and Michelle Zhang, with Hull, Woad and Ewart Shadoff part of the logjam sharing fifth of 10 under.

Ewart Shadoff birdied her first three holes on her way to a second-round 66 and Woad mixed six birdies with one bogey to post the same score, while Hull carded a bogey-free 67 to also stay in the chasing pack.

Former AIG Women's Open champion Miyu Yamashita is in the group on nine under containing Julia Lopez Ramirez, part of Europe's victorious Solheim Cup team earlier this month, while Mimi Rhodes and Leona Maguire were among the players to miss the cut.

articles.title: South Florida beats Bowling Green 14-6 to improve to 4-0 for the first time since 2018
articles.summary: D.J. Crowther rushed for 143 yards and a touchdown, and South Florida scored 14 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to beat Bowling Green 14-6 on Saturda...
articles.body:
BOWLING GREEN, Ohio (AP) — D.J. Crowther rushed for 143 yards and a touchdown, and South Florida scored 14 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to beat Bowling Green 14-6 on Saturday.

USF's first two drives of the second half resulted in 22 yards of offense in 11 plays. The next two went 13 plays for 116 yards and 14 points.

USF forced a turnover on downs early in the fourth quarter and then used six plays to go 44 yards, ending in a 2-yard touchdown run for Luke Kromenhoek . It was his third rushing touchdown in the last two games.

Crowther capped the scoring after a six-play, 72-yard drive ended in a 1-yard score with 5:34 left.

Bowling Green came up just short on a fourth-and-16 play in the final seconds.

Michael Van Buren Jr. was 7-of-11 passing for 52 yards for South Florida, which improved to 4-0 for the first time since 2018. The Bulls entered Saturday one of 35 unbeaten teams in the Football Bowl Subdivision.

Jay Kastantin was 16 of 28 for 122 yards passing for Bowling Green (0-4), which entered among 13 winless teams in FBS.

When the Bulls last faced Bowling Green in 2002, the Falcons were ranked No. 25 in the coaches' poll under the direction of coach Urban Meyer.

South Florida: Returns home to play Temple next Saturday.

Bowling Green: Plays at Miami (Ohio) next Saturday.

articles.title: New Green Card rules that came into effect starting this September: List of categories subject to the changes and those that are not impacted
articles.summary: Starting this month (September, 2026) the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) implemented new guidance on the public change inadmissibility
articles.body: Starting this month (September, 2026) the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) implemented new guidance on the public change inadmissibility determination. The rules expanded the requirement for most Green Card applicants to demonstrate financial independence, while exempting humanitarian categories such as refugees and victims of trafficking. The new rules apply to a wide range of applicants, particularly those seeking permanent residency through family or employment pathways.New Green Card rules: Categories subject to the new changeMost people applying to adjust their status to lawful permanent residence remain subject to public charge review under the new guidance. This includes spouses, children, and parents of U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents, as well as other qualifying relatives; fiancé(e)s of U.S. citizens; priority workers, professionals with advanced degrees, and individuals of exceptional ability; skilled workers, other professionals, and general workers under employment-based categories; investors; religious workers; and diversity visa immigrants. USCIS has specifically reiterated that children are not exempt from the public charge ground of inadmissibility, closing off a potential point of confusion for family-based applicants.Categories exemptHumanitarian and special categories remain unaffected by the new rules. Exempt groups include:* Refugees and asylees* Victims of trafficking (T visas) and qualifying criminal activity (U visas)* Special immigrant juveniles* VAWA survivors* Afghan and Iraqi interpreters or nationals employed by the U.S. government* Cuban, Haitian, Nicaraguan, and Central American entrants* Certain diplomats, broadcasters, and applicants under special immigration laws.What role the I-864 affidavit still playsThe Form I-864, Affidavit of Support, continues to play an important role in the process, though USCIS has clarified that submitting a qualifying I-864 alone does not automatically establish that an applicant isn't inadmissible on public charge grounds. For family-based immigrants and certain employment-based immigrants, failing to submit a sufficient I-864 can itself result in a public charge inadmissibility finding, and officers may also evaluate whether the sponsor listed is realistically able and willing to provide the financial support they've committed to.USCIS has also noted that a few individual circumstances shouldn't, on their own, trigger a negative public charge determination — periods of unemployment, age, and disability are not supposed to automatically count against an applicant, particularly if the individual is otherwise healthy and willing and able to work.Which filing date determines which rules applyPerhaps the most important practical detail for applicants is the transition timeline, since USCIS adjudicates based on when an application was postmarked or submitted electronically, not when it's reviewed:* On or after September 18, 2026: The new 2026 guidance applies, with its broader list of considered benefits.* December 23, 2022 through September 17, 2026: The narrower 2022 Final Rule and its more limited benefits list apply.* Before December 23, 2022: The original 1999 Interim Field Guidance applies.This means the exact same set of facts — for example, a green card holder's spouse who received SNAP benefits several years ago — could lead to a different outcome purely depending on which filing window the application falls into, making the submission date itself a significant factor for applicants navigating the new system.A bond option remains availableIf USCIS determines an applicant is inadmissible solely on public charge grounds, the agency retains discretion to allow the individual to post a Public Charge Bond using Form I-945 as a financial guarantee, rather than being automatically denied — an option that predates the current changes but remains part of the updated guidance moving forward.You use AI every day. articles.title: Presidents Cup: Brandt Snedeker reveals captaincy criticisms ahead of singles as Team USA look to avoid Medinah upset
articles.summary: Can Team USA avoid a shock home defeat at the Presidents Cup? How the International Team are closing on history but have a big final day ahead at Medinah; watch the Sunday singles live from 4.30pm on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Team USA came into the week as overwhelming favourites to claim a record-extending 11th consecutive victory, in a biennial event where much of the pre-tournament narrative was around whether change was needed to make it more competitive.

Next to no hope had been given to Geoff Ogilvy's International Team, who earned their only Presidents Cup win in 1998 and have lost every edition since a 17-17 tie in 2003, but they are now five points away from completing a seismic shock at Medinah.

A clean sweep in the Friday foursomes gave the visitors a 7-3 advantage heading into Saturday's double session, where the Internationals saw the leaderboard filled with red numbers in both - indicating American leads - before delivering late fightbacks.

The Internationals claimed a share of the spoils in the afternoon foursomes to take a 10.5-7.5 advantage into the Sunday singles, just the fourth time they've led heading into the final day of a Presidents Cup and first experience of it on American soil.

"It's tough when there's all red on the board, but to get 2-2 out of that afternoon session and to go into tomorrow with a lead, which was the goal at the start of the week, I'm very proud of them," Ogilvy said.

Team USA have been outpointed in foursomes for a second successive Presidents Cup and have been dominated on the par-threes around Medinah, with the International Team holding a 25-6 advantage on those holes.

Snedeker's strategy and pairings have come under scrutiny, with Russell Henley and Jacob Bridgeman a winless foursomes pairing in two sessions and Wyndham Clark returning just one point from his four matches so far.

Scottie Scheffler's torrid foursomes record for Team USA continued alongside Sam Burns, leading to him being benched on Saturday afternoon, with a frazzled Snedeker even getting muddled by his own selections during a live TV interview.

"I tried to work my tail off to put these guys in the best situation possible and I don't think I've done a very good job this week, to be where we are right now," Snedeker admitted in his press conference.

"They [Team USA] look to me to put them in the best position where they're comfortable. I hold myself to a high standard - I don't think I've done the best job for them in that room.

"They've given me everything I could possibly ask for and I've just got to figure out ways to get these guys in better situations. I don't think I've held up my end of the bargain. The guys have done everything I've asked of them so far."

It would be somewhat fitting if the Internationals could close out an elusive away victory on Sunday at Medinah, 14 years on from Team Europe producing their own unlikely success over Team USA at the same venue.

Europe's comeback from 10-4 down to win 14.5-13.5 in 2012 was miraculous enough for it to be the 'Miracle at Medinah', although their pre-tournament hopes had been far stronger that week than what was expected from the International Team here.

There are still 40 per cent of the week's points on offer to be won on the final day, meaning the narrative can quickly change, while the Internationals have failed to reach five points in singles at two of the last three Presidents Cups.

Three points is a far friendlier deficit to overcome than the United States faced at last year's Ryder Cup, where they briefly threatened to come back from seven behind before Europe eventually survived their scare to win 15-13.

Team USA picked up 8.5 points in singles that day and require another big return on Sunday, with 7.5 points needed simply to retain the trophy and eight points for outright victory.

"I like the spot we're in better than we were last year," said Cameron Young, who will lead out Team USA like he did 12 months ago. "A lot of the feelings are the same. These team events bring out a different side of all of us and a different side of golf."

Justin Thomas and Scheffler have also been sent out in early matches, while Ogilvy has resisted the urge to top-load his side by putting many of his star players in the anchor ties.

Team USA appeared to have the pre-tournament edge in world rankings, PGA Tour success and squad depth, with Snedeker still hopeful his side can continue a winning run that has seen them claim 13 of the previous 15 editions.

"A lot can happen on these Sundays," Snedeker insisted. "We've seen it happen a lot over the last couple of years. I think we're going to draw on what happened last year at the Ryder Cup and how close we came to that big comeback.

"There's plenty of evidence that these things are never over. You've got to show up ready to go. I think our guys are champing at the bit to get out there."

There has been no point in history where Team USA haven't been the defending champions in at least one of the Ryder Cup, Solheim Cup, Walker Cup or Presidents Cup.

Given their humbling Ryder Cup loss in New York last year, their Solheim Cup defeat in the Netherlands earlier this month and their Walker Cup defeat to Great Britain and Ireland, a big Sunday is required to stop the Presidents Cup also leaving their grasp.

articles.title: Crawley homes without water and roads closed after burst pipe
articles.summary: Southern Water says it is investigating the burst pipe which happened on Sunday morning.
articles.body:
Thousands of homes in parts of Crawley have water supply issues and a number of roads have flooded after what police are describing as a "significant" leak.

Roads around the Southgate Roundabout in Crawley have been closed on Sunday morning due to the burst water pipe, Sussex Police said.

Southern Water said around 9,000 customers were impacted and it was setting up bottled water stations.

A company spokesperson said: "Our teams are on site and working as quickly and safely as possible to repair the burst and restore supplies."

The company said customers were experiencing a loss of water supply or low pressure in the following areas - Woolborough Road, Holmcroft, Southgate, Tilgate and Furnace Green.

The Southern Water spokesperson added: "Restoring water to customers as quickly as possible remains our highest priority."

Southgate Avenue, Crawley Avenue and part of the A23 are currently closed, according to the company.

Sussex Police has asked that people avoid the area while emergency services manage the situation safely.

Martin Lawrence was making deliveries in the area at 05:00 BST.

He told BBC Radio Sussex : "I came across this massive flood going across the road.

"There was a large amount of water going from one side of the roundabout to the other and going into an underpass.

"I've never seen so much water in my life."

articles.title: Will Packers avoid facing Bears QB Caleb Williams in Week 5?
articles.summary: It's currently unclear if Caleb Williams, who has a hamstring injury, will be healed in time to face the Packers in Week 5.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers may avoid Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams when the two long-time rivals meet in Week 5. According to new reporting from Adam Schefter of ESPN and Ian Rapoport of NFL Network , Williams has a Grade 2 hamstring injury and could miss 3-4 weeks, based on normal recovery timelines of similar injuries, although there is some optimism that he will return to the field sooner rather than later.

The Packers and Bears face off at Lambeau Field on Sunday, Oct. 11, or 14 days from Sunday. Williams was originally hurt on Sunday, Sept. 20 against the Minnesota Vikings . If Williams actually misses three weeks of practice and games, he will not play against the Packers in Week 5. More than likely, Williams would need to return to practice in some capacity during the next two weeks to have a realistic shot at facing the Packers.

The Bears already ruled out Williams for Monday night's showdown with the Philadelphia Eagles . Chicago will start Tyson Bagent if he clears concussion protocol or veteran Case Keenum if Bagent isn't available, but with a backup quarterback under center, the Bears are in danger of a 1-2 start.

Injuries will be in the spotlight in Week 5. It's currently unclear if the Packers will have edge rusher Micah Parsons -- who is eligible to come off the PUP list as soon as Week 5 -- available to play against the Bears. Parsons can start practicing at any point over the next two weeks.

There's an outside chance that both Parsons and Williams could return from injuries for the Week 5 showdown. The more likely scenario is that both players miss the game and neither team is at full strength for the important early season rivalry game.

Last season, Williams led the Bears to comeback wins over the Packers in Week 16 and the NFC Wild Card Round. Both games were at Soldier Field. Keisean Nixon 's leaping interception of Williams in the end zone prevented a Bears comeback during a win at Lambeau Field, the Packers' last win of the 2025 season.

articles.title: Tom Kim, de la Presidents Cup a los Juegos Asiáticos para tratar de evitar el servicio militar obligatorio
articles.standfirst: El surcoreano disputa el segundo partido individual en Medinah y ser marchará a Japón en cuanto termine de jugar, por lo que no podría celebrar una hipotética victoria del Equipo Internacional
articles.summary: El surcoreano disputa el segundo partido individual en Medinah y ser marchará a Japón en cuanto termine de jugar, por lo que no podría celebrar una hipotética victoria del Equipo Internacional
articles.body: El Equipo Internacional cuenta con buenas opciones de ganar la Presidents Cup a Estados Unidos, dado que el resultado antes de los 12 duelos individuales es de 10,5 a 7,5. En caso de victoria sería un triunfo histórico, ya que el equipo de los internacionales, capitaneados en esta edición por Geoff Ogilvy, lo lograrían por primera vez en 28 años. Sin embargo, una de las estrellas de este equipo, el surcoreano Tom Kim, es probable que no esté presente para celebrar este hipotético éxito. Kim, que ha ganado tres de sus cuatro partidos esta semana en Medinah (Chicago), viajará en cuanto termine su duelo individual a Japón. El surcoreano de 24 años, que se enfrentará al estadounidense Wyndham Clark en el segundo de los 12 partidos individuales, quiere hacer todo lo posible por llegar cuantos a su siguiente competición, el torneo de los Juegos Asiáticos que comienza el miércoles en el Kasugai Country Club (Kasugai, prefectura de Aichi, Japón). El caso es que una medalla de oro en la competición masculina o en la competición por equipos eximiría a Kim del servicio militar obligatorio. Según la legislación surcoreana, los hombres aptos para hacer la mili, salvo contadas excepciones, deben cumplir entre 18 y 21 meses de servicio. Se conceden exenciones especiales a los atletas y artistas que destacan en ciertos tipos de competiciones internacionales vinculadas al prestigio nacional. En el caso de los deportistas, estamos hablando de cualquier medalla en los Juegos Olímpicos o una medalla de oro en los Juegos Asiáticos. Ahora mismo Corea del Sur es la favorita junto a Japón para hacerse con el oro por equipos en golf, pero a título individual no cabe duda de que Tom Kim –con 13 triunfos profesionales, cuatro de ellos en el PGA Tour- puede luchar también por el metal dorado. En los Juegos Olímpicos de París se quedó a cuatro golpes del bronce y, por tanto, aún no está exento del servicio militar pese a ser un golfista contrastado. Por suerte los Juegos Asiáticos, que antes eran para amateur, permitieron la participación de profesionales en su última edición, que había sido pospuesta hasta 2023 debido a la pandemia. Sungjae Im y Si Woo Kim fueron los profesionales seleccionados por Corea del Sur y ganaron la medalla de oro en la competición por equipos.

articles.title: Open de France: Matt Fitzpatrick closes out three-shot victory at Le Golf National to earn fourth worldwide win of 2026
articles.summary: Matt Fitzpatrick carded a final-round 70 at Le Golf National to close out FedEx Open de France victory and claim a first DP World Tour win of the season; Fitzpatrick had already won three times on the PGA Tour in 2026
articles.body:
The world No 4 took a five-shot advantage into the final day and never relinquished control, mixing two birdies and one bogey in a final-round 70 that saw him register an 11th DP World Tour title.

Fitzpatrick ended the week on 20 under and comfortably ahead of closest challenger Angel Hidalgo, who birdied three of his last five holes to card a final-round 67, while Eugenio Chacarra was among the group five back in a share of third.

Chacarra closed the gap on Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy at the top of the Race to Dubai rankings with his latest strong showing, with Tom Vaillant, Matthieu Pavon and Ryder Cup hopeful Kristoffer Reitan the others on 15 under.

Fitzpatrick had already won the Valspar Championship, RBC Hertiage and Zurich Classic of New Orleans on the PGA Tour this year, while his latest DP World Tour success is his first since the DP World Tour Championship in November.

How Fitzpatrick completed Open de France victory

The Englishman's sizeable overnight lead was quickly reduced when Chacarra, playing in the group ahead, followed three birdies in his first four holes by adding another from 12 feet at the par-four sixth.

Chacarra cancelled out a three-putt bogey from long range at the eighth by taking advantage of the par-five next, lifting him back within two of Fitzpatrick after the former US Open champion made par on every hole on his front nine.

Reitan also got within three of Fitzpatrick after racing to the turn in 33 and birdieing the par-five 14th, only for the Norwegian's hopes to unravel with bogeys on two of his next three holes.

Chacarra's title challenge was derailed when he was forced to take a drop after an errant tee shot at the 13th, then found water with his third shot, leaving the Spaniard having to get up and down from the drop zone to scramble a double bogey.

Fitzpatrick then regained full control of the tournament when he fired his approach at the 13th to kick-in range and rolled in from 20 feet at the 15th, with those birdies lifting him to 21 under and five clear.

Stress-free pars over the next two holes kept Fitzpatrick in control heading to the par-four last, where he failed to get up and down from just off the green but tapped in to close out victory with a bogey.

"Obviously delighted to get over the line," Fitzpatrick said. "It was definitely a battle today. Didn't have my best stuff for the first 12 holes and then managed to find some of my best stuff.

"Golf is a game of multiple skills and I used them all in the end this week. Just coming down the stretch there, to get the shots I did and make the putts I did was special."

Hidalgo's runner-up finish qualified him for The Open at St Andrews next summer via The Open Qualifying Series, with Fitzpatrick already exempt, as Vaillant jumped into tied-third after holing a 20-foot birdie on the final hole.

First-round leader Michael Kim shared seventh place with Guido Migliozzi and Brandon Stone, while Ludvig Åberg moved into tied-11th after a five-under 66 on the final day.

The DP World Tour heads to Scotland for the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship, played across Carnoustie, Kingsbarns Golf Links and the Old Course at St Andrews, where Robert MacIntyre is defending champion.

England's Matt Fitzpatrick secured his fourth title of the season with a three-shot win at the French Open in Paris.

Fitzpatrick carded a one-under-par 70 to hold off the challenge of Spain's Angel Hidalgo at Le Golf National.

The 32-year-old has already won the Valspar Championship and RBC Heritage titles on the PGA Tour this year, as well as the Zurich Classic team event in New Orleans alongside younger brother Alex.

He led by five shots going into the final day, but a run of 12 successive pars allowed the chasing pack to cut that advantage to two.

However, crucial birdies on the 13th and 15th pushed Fitzpatrick further clear and even a bogey at the last could not deny him an 11th European Tour title.

"Delighted to get it over the line, it was definitely a battle today," he said.

"I didn't have my best stuff for the first 12 holes and then managed to find some of my best stuff.

"In a way I was quite lucky - I left myself in some nice spots where you can still get up and down from, but I fully took advantage of that and did really well."

Matthieu Pavon shot the best round of the day, with a seven-under 64 ensuring he finished tied for fourth alongside French compatriot Tom Vaillant, Spain's Eugenio Lopez-Chacarra and Norway's Kristoffer Reitan.
